name: Digital Twin Explorer
description: The /digital-twin Explorer — four tabs (Completeness, the default; Lifecycle; Delivery; UI Bridge) over a 59-row manifest taxonomy of the twin of the software-development process: the completeness matrix + the cell-detail interactive flow + the Lifecycle-tab stage pipeline + the Delivery-tab verdict lookup (coord#634/web#587, hardened by web#609/#612/#614, UI-Bridge-instrumented by web#617 and later changes for the Delivery card and the Lifecycle tab). ci-bot is a superuser so the authed page renders. Route stubs make the page deterministic without live coord: GET /api/v1/digital-twin/catalog (coord's served catalog: the 18 sub-spaces it declares probeable — 17 snapshot:true rows plus the envelope-shaped admin outbound door — and three it does not, so the page joins the manifest to it) and GET /api/v1/digital-twin/subspaces (the probe of exactly those 18, restricted:false; worktree, train_activity, merge_economics and secrets_broker are report doors and read 'served') set the cells' credibility/status for both the matrix and the Lifecycle view, GET /api/v1/digital-twin/subspace/twin_fidelity/raw answers 404 (coord serves no twin_fidelity probe yet) so the Completeness tab's Twin self-fidelity header reads UNKNOWN, GET /api/v1/digital-twin/subspace/schema/raw returns a DriftVerdict so the Schema drawer's 'Show raw data' toggle (gated on readsRaw && verdict) renders, and GET /api/v1/digital-twin/delivery/verdict answers the Delivery lookup. Assertions target the web#617 useUIElement ids (digital-twin-tab-*, digital-twin-cell-*, digital-twin-show-raw), which resolve against the UI-Bridge registry the matcher reads; the page titles ('Digital Twin', 'Ask the Twin') resolve via the wrapper's content-discovery pass (provider.tsx contentDiscovery enabled). STRUCTURE NOTE: spec-ci's structural lane evaluates every state against the INITIAL render, so only initially-present states are declared (shell + matrix). Tab switches, the Lifecycle pipeline (digital-twin-stage-<stage>, cells digital-twin-stage-<stage>-cell-<id> — stage-scoped because a row shows under every stage it observes) and the cell -> drawer -> raw-verdict interaction are transitions with activateStates:[] whose waitAfter conditions are the pass condition. Radix Tabs unmounts inactive content, so every tab-switch transition switches back to Completeness before it ends, and all of them run BEFORE the drawer transition (the drawer is a modal Dialog that would block a tab click and needs the matrix mounted). CI runs with NO connected runner, so Ask-the-Twin and the UI Bridge tab show their 'Connect a runner' empty states — their runner-only input ids (ask-the-twin-*, ui-bridge-*) do NOT mount and are NOT asserted; no transition here needs a runner. Read-only; structural.

entries.description: Per-surface release/deploy freshness (ecs / vercel / npm / github_releases — the runner installer publish) — is a given commit/tag live?
Alembic migration head vs applied revisions; coord.* schema table-set reconciliation.
Declared-vs-actual infrastructure drift (task definitions, service state).
Live availability + performance (declared-SLO-vs-live-metric) drift.
Composed effective feature-flag / config state (armed-but-inert verdicts).
Per-surface runtime self-health (the killer-query companion to is_commit_live).
Cross-repo dependency state — versions, install/publish safety inputs.
Declared-vs-actual route-serving drift (route manifest vs a live edge probe).
Per-surface client-telemetry 4-invariant drift (the prod-browser boundary).
Per-tenant agentic-memory store state — rows, bytes, embedding coverage, quota.

Live worktree disk census per device — git identity, dirtiness, the target/ and node_modules/ space sinks, build-target provenance and declared-vs-undeclared counts. Bound to the caller: a device reads its own, an operator its tenant's.

Background-worker loop liveness: last tick, outcome, decision code and error streak per (worker, replica), rolled up fleet-true to alive / stale / dead / not_leader_here. Answers "is worker X frozen?" directly instead of inferring it from missing log lines.

FLEET-WIDE merge-train enumeration — one row per coord-authority repo, INCLUDING repos with NO merge proposals, which every other train read structurally omits (/pr-merge/health joins the proposal tables and is TenantId-gated; train_health above needs a repo you already suspect). Ask THIS first to find the repo, then train_health for its physics. Per repo: authority (canonical_repos vs tenant_repos, which differ and are checked by different routes), activity_kind, open / open-non-draft PR counts, a verdict_histogram keyed on classify_merge_status's own tokens, and `triage` — of whose six values TWO are alarms, both built on a positive statement rather than an absence: `idle_unserved` (coord judges a PR landable and has accepted nothing) and `halted` (the merge scheduler has recorded a SUSTAINED tenant_ci_fleet_offline run for this repo — its pre-push gate kept refusing the repo's candidates; since qontinui-coord#1869 no configured path closes that gate and the default 48 h trace ring holds no older row, so a live run means the gate closed again, a coord defect to investigate; served with the run itself in `halt_run`). Counts are null, never 0, when unmeasured.

Per-repo merge economics — candidate-CI duration (T), land rate (λ), λ·T pressure, waste (CI minutes per land), a data-driven stuck-PR threshold, and arming_coverage (how many landed PRs carried an arming record for the head that landed).

Is GitHub still DELIVERING webhooks? Per-(repo, event_type) counters + last_received_at, with a `gap` verdict when a CI-bearing event type goes silent while the repo has fresh (stale-orphan-filtered) in-flight CI — the lost-webhook wedge class, made queryable instead of inferred from missing log lines.

Merge-scheduler decision traces — what each tick/land outcome DECIDED and why (landed / waiting_ci / deferred:<reason> / budget_backoff:<surface> / tick_error:<class> / tick_degraded:<n>). Ask this instead of inferring a freeze from log silence.
Ξ_Outbound — coord's OWN outbound-dependency budget/health (GitHub quota burn, cool-down, stale-serve doom-loop). 'Is coord burning its quota?' in one query.

Secrets broker — the op catalog, credential inventory with rotation_due, the principal exposure matrix, recent ops grouped by agent session, mints, and pending operator actions. References, metadata and keyed fingerprints; value-shaped residual refused at coord ingest.
Has a work unit actually landed? work-unit ⋈ per-PR merged-state ⋈ deploy.

Live CI state for a repo/PR (rollup, required-check status, no-reap gate). `ref` DEFAULTS TO 'main', so this is also the live per-repo read for "is main red right now?" — it recomputes against the Actions API rather than reading coord.ci_baselines, which makes it the way to RESOLVE a main verdict coord reports as unknown. One repo per call; for the fleet-wide per-repo green/red/unknown enumeration use coord_diagnose's `main_ci` component.
Self-fidelity report — where the twin's model diverges from reality.

states.name: Explorer shell + tabs
states.description: The /digital-twin chrome that renders on the default Completeness tab: the page title, the four tab triggers (Completeness / Lifecycle / Delivery / UI Bridge — registered via useUIElement ids; the Lifecycle trigger's assertion is appended last so the earlier assertion indices stay stable), and the 'Ask the Twin' section heading (which renders in both the runner and no-runner branches — in CI there is no runner, so its input/submit controls do not mount and are not asserted). Identifies the page mounted, authenticated, not redirected.

assertions.description: h1 'Digital Twin' — the page title proving the section mounted (authed, not redirected). Resolves via content-discovery.
'Ask the Twin' section heading (h2; renders in both the runner and no-runner branches). Resolves via content-discovery.
Lifecycle tab trigger (id digital-twin-tab-lifecycle) — the second tab, the stage pipeline of the twin of the software-development process.

states.name: Completeness matrix cells
states.description: The sub-space cells the matrix renders from the 59-row manifest taxonomy (the matrix denominator), joined with the stubbed GET /subspaces probe for live status. Each cell is registered with a web#617 useUIElement id digital-twin-cell-<manifestId>; this state asserts a representative set across status classes: schema (snapshot, implemented — the drawer-transition target), infra (snapshot, implemented), deps (snapshot, the 'blind' class). settleUntilPresent waits for digital-twin-cell-schema to register before the matcher snapshots, dodging the probe/render load race.

assertions.description: Schema sub-space cell (id digital-twin-cell-schema) — the drawer-transition target.
Deps sub-space cell (id digital-twin-cell-deps) — the 'blind' status class.

transitions.name: Delivery tab: switch, look up a work-unit, read the verdict
transitions.description: Behavioral READ of the Delivery tab (shipped by plan 2026-06-15-twin-delivery-verdict-completion-view): (1) click the Delivery tab trigger (id digital-twin-tab-delivery) -> the DeliveryVerdictCard mounts, asserted by its lookup input (id digital-twin-delivery-input) appearing; (2) type a work-unit slug into that input; (3) click 'Look up' (id digital-twin-delivery-submit) -> the stubbed GET /digital-twin/delivery/verdict resolves and the verdict block renders, asserted by its 'Show raw data' toggle (id digital-twin-delivery-show-raw, gated on verdict && summary) appearing; (4) switch back to the Completeness tab (id digital-twin-tab-completeness) so the matrix remounts for the open-drawer transition that follows (Radix Tabs unmounts inactive content). The DeliveryVerdictCard controls were instrumented with stable useUIElement ids in this same change (they previously had none). activateStates is empty; the transition passes iff every action executes and each waitAfter resolves. The type action's idle waitAfter lets React flush so the submit button is enabled before the click. Runs FIRST (and restores Completeness) so it does not collide with the modal Dialog the open-drawer transition opens. Needs no connected runner (delivery is coord-backed and stubbed here).

transitions.name: Lifecycle tab: switch, see the stage pipeline, switch back
transitions.description: Behavioral READ of the Lifecycle tab (the twin of the software-development process laid over intent → plan → implement → verify → integrate → release → operate → learn): (1) click the Lifecycle tab trigger (id digital-twin-tab-lifecycle) -> LifecycleView mounts one section per stage, each registered with a useUIElement id digital-twin-stage-<stage>; the pass condition is the Verify stage section (id digital-twin-stage-verify) appearing. The sections render from the checked-in manifest joined with the stubbed GET /subspaces probe, so they mount whatever the probe answers (only a restricted:true probe would replace them with the access notice; the stub sends restricted:false). Cells in this view carry stage-scoped ids (digital-twin-stage-<stage>-cell-<id>) because a row shows under every stage it observes, and the matrix's digital-twin-cell-<id> ids are unmounted while this tab is open. (2) switch back to the Completeness tab (id digital-twin-tab-completeness) so the matrix remounts for the open-drawer transition that follows (Radix Tabs unmounts inactive content), asserted by digital-twin-cell-schema reappearing. activateStates is empty; the transition passes iff every action executes and each waitAfter resolves. Runs after the Delivery lookup and BEFORE the open-drawer transition, so it never collides with the modal Dialog that transition opens. Needs no connected runner (the probe is coord-backed and stubbed here).

transitions.name: Open the Schema sub-space drawer (cell click)
transitions.description: Behavioral READ: click the Schema sub-space cell (id digital-twin-cell-schema). The detail Dialog opens; because schema is query_kind 'snapshot' and the stubbed GET /subspace/schema/raw returns a verdict, the 'Show raw data' toggle (id digital-twin-show-raw, gated on readsRaw && verdict) renders. The waitAfter on that toggle appearing is the pass condition — proving the cell -> drawer -> raw-verdict flow works end-to-end. activateStates is empty (the structural lane only models the initial render), so this transition passes iff the click executes without error AND show-raw appears within the timeout. Needs no connected runner (the matrix + drawer are coord-backed and stubbed here).
